caveats: an induced conflict proves the loop recovers from a serialization failure; it does not predict how often Cloud produces one under real load
the local single-node cluster also produces 40001 for a deliberate write-after-read conflict, so this probe is not by itself evidence of anything Cloud-specific

payload.honest_note: the bulk load wrote disjoint primary keys, one transaction per batch, and observed 0 serialization failure(s) across 20 batch(es). A zero there is the expected result of an uncontended load, and on its own it is indistinguishable from a loop that does not work — which is why the induced probe exists and is reported separately. The two numbers are never added: one measures the workload, the other measures the loop.

cloud.label: cloud/induced-write-after-read
cloud.method: transaction A reads k=1; transaction B commits an update to k=1; transaction A then writes k=1 and commits — a write-after-read conflict, which CockroachDB refuses under SERIALIZABLE with SQLSTATE 40001

local.label: local/induced-write-after-read
local.method: transaction A reads k=1; transaction B commits an update to k=1; transaction A then writes k=1 and commits — a write-after-read conflict, which CockroachDB refuses under SERIALIZABLE with SQLSTATE 40001

loop.backoff: full jitter over a linearly growing window: sleep(min(2.0, 0.05 * retry) * (0.5 + random()))
loop.non_retryable: every other SQLSTATE is re-raised unchanged; a gate refusal (23514, P0001) is a result in this system and retrying it would be a way of asking the same forbidden question eight times
